newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG soldiers release defence chief.
newsitem.headline: PNG soldiers release defence chief.

text.p: Papua New Guinea soldiers on Monday freed the country's defence chief from house arrest after holding him captive all day, a senior army officer said.

Major Walter Enuma said defence force commander Brigadier Colonel Leo Nuia had been released after the prime minister ordered charges against troops involved in a March army revolt be withheld pending a new inquiry into a mercenary deal.
"We are implementing the prime minister's directive (to release the commander) straight away and I expect the other party to honour its commitment," Enuma told reporters.
Soldiers arrested Nuia on Monday morning after earlier freeing Enuma from a police cell where he was awaiting a court appearance on firearm charges related to the June election.
The soldiers had demanded a general amnesty for all troops involved in a March revolt against African mercenaries hired to end the secessionist rebellion on Bougainville island.

Local media have reported that the commander of the revolt, former Brigadier General Jerry Singirok, will be charged with sedition on his return to Papua New Guinea on Tuesday. Enuma was Singirok's right-hand man and commanded the operation to throw the mercenaries out of the South Pacific nation.
The mercernaries, subsequently expelled, had been brought in to help put down an insurrection on the island of Bougainville.
